title: When Love Grows Cold
paragraphs:
When Love Grows Cold
A chilling sign of the last days.
— Matthew 24:12
It doesn’t happen all at once.

Not with thunder.
Not with headlines.
Not with a warning siren screaming in your ear.
It happens quietly.
Love… fades.
Jesus said it straight—no filter, no softening:
“Because lawlessness will multiply, the love of many will grow cold.” — Matthew 24:12
Did you catch that?

Not some.
Not a few.
Many.

That means this isn’t just about the world out there.
This is about hearts in here.

Church seats.
Prayer rooms.
Quiet lives that once burned.
Cold.
And here’s the tension we don’t want to admit:

You can still smile… and be freezing inside.
You can still serve… and be slowly disconnecting.
You can still say “God is good”… while your heart whispers, “I feel nothing.”
That’s how dangerous this is.
Because when sin becomes normal, love becomes optional.

Lawlessness isn’t just crime in the streets.
It’s rebellion in the soul.

It’s when truth becomes negotiable.
When conviction becomes inconvenience.
When holiness becomes “too much.”
And little by little…

Love for God becomes routine.
Love for people becomes selective.
Love for truth becomes silent.
Until one day—you realize:

You’re still there…
but the fire is gone.
Let me say something heavy, but necessary:
Cold hearts don’t start cold. They drift there.

One compromise.
One hidden sin.
One offense you refused to release.
One moment you chose comfort over obedience.
And suddenly, what used to move you… no longer does.

Worship feels like noise.
Prayer feels like effort.
The Word feels distant.
That’s not just fatigue.
That’s spiritual frost.

But here’s where the story shifts—
because Jesus didn’t just warn us…
He made a way back.
Listen carefully.

The same chapter that speaks of cold love…
points us to enduring faith.

The problem is real.
But so is the solution.

Because at the center of history stands a Man on a cross—
bleeding, broken, yet burning with unstoppable love.
While humanity was at its worst…
He didn’t grow cold.
He forgave.
“Father, forgive them…” (Luke 23:34)
He stayed.
He endured.
He loved to the very end.

That is not weak love.
That is redeeming love.
And that love is still alive today.

So if you feel distant…
if your heart feels numb…
if your fire has turned into ashes…
Hear this clearly:
You are not too far gone.
Cold is not your final state.

Because Jesus doesn’t just save sinners—
He revives hearts.

He restores what sin froze.
He reignites what compromise buried.
He calls you back—not with shame, but with grace.
But you must respond.
This is not the hour to stay passive.
This is the hour to:

Return to prayer—even when it feels dry.
Return to the Word—even when it feels silent.
Return to repentance—especially when it’s uncomfortable.
Because warmth returns where surrender begins.
Let the Holy Spirit search you.

Not to condemn you—
but to awaken you.
Ask yourself:

When was the last time I truly burned for God?
When was the last time His presence mattered more than my comfort?
When was the last time I chose holiness… even when no one was watching?
Don’t ignore those questions.
They are not accusations.
They are invitations.
Because in a world growing colder by the day…
God is raising people who refuse to freeze.

People who will love when it’s hard.
Stand when it’s costly.
Stay faithful when others drift.
People whose hearts stay close to Jesus—no matter the season.
This is your moment.

Not tomorrow.
Not someday.
Now.
Come back to the fire.
Come back to the cross.
Come back to the One whose love never changes.
Because even if the love of many grows cold…
His love for you never will.
And that love is not just comfort.
It’s a call.

A call to repent.
A call to believe.
A call to follow Jesus fully—no halfway, no holding back.
Because the end is not about fear.
It’s about faithfulness.

Prayer:
Lord Jesus, if my heart has grown cold, awaken me again. Burn away every compromise, every hidden sin, every distraction. Restore my love for You. Teach me to walk in truth, to love deeply, and to stay faithful in these last days. I choose You again—fully, completely, without reserve. In Jesus’ name, amen.
Send it to someone who needs the fire back.
Because someone out there is freezing…
…and this might be the spark that brings them home.
